column2: `design.plan_drafter` / `step2b_drafter_main` picks one vendor (env override, else codex-if-present else claude), not a sequential codex→claude waterfall. routing it through `external_defaults.tool_order()` risks multi-tier attempts and changes failure/fallback semantics versus live `python/design_lifecycle.py:3500-3502`.

live `review_pipeline.py` adds `--no-fallback` only when both vendors are present **and** `round_num < 2` (round 1 only); generic codex still runs in rounds 1 and 2. a registry that stores only slot tools or a blanket no-fallback flag can enable fallback in round 1 or disable/widen it in round 2, changing panel semantics.

live `voterslotpolicy` carries `primary_tool`, fixed `output_name`, prompt labels, and per-tool `semantic_labels`; voter 1 is cursor-direct with claude replacement (no codex), not a three-tier waterfall, and switches output file (`cursor-validity-vote-output.txt` vs `claude-vote-output.txt`) when cursor is absent. a thin `slotdefault` or registry `tool_order("review.voters")` can break prompt rendering, collector filenames, and reintroduce forbidden codex fallback on slot 1.

`aggregate_partition` hardcodes `{"tool": "codex"}` for the aggregator slot (`decompose.py:608`); plan wording treats inclusion as optional, so this dispatch can remain outside the registry and evade per-role pinning in `test_external_role_defaults.py`.

today an invalid override (e.g. `larch_design_drafter=invalid vendor`) sets `skip_reason` and skips the drafter launch, then falls through to inline drafting (`design_lifecycle.py:3505-3506`, `3537`, `3691`). if the new resolver raises on bad values, step 2b fallback regresses and plan drafting can stop instead of preserving soft fallback.

both `scout dynamic-archetypes` and `scout plan-archetypes` → `scout_plan_archetypes` call the shared `scout_dynamic_archetypes` waterfall. if the refactor reads only one registry role (`review.dynamic_archetype_scout` or `design.plan_archetype_scout`), changing one role in tests would not protect the other live path.

skills/design/references/brainstorm.md:52 [scope-reduction] `design.brainstorm_pragmatic` as a registry role adds surface without a dispatch site. scenario: pragmatic brainstorm is always parent-session claude per the slot table; registry/cli lookup buys nothing and expands `test_external_role_defaults.py`

`design.plan_voters` must not be wired through `agent_voters.py` or reuse `review.voters` `voterpolicydefault` rows. live plan voters dispatch only from `plan_review_panel.dispatch_voters` (v1 claude, v2 codex, v3 cursor; distinct output basenames). routing plan voters through `agent_voters` / `review.voters` would flip tools, collectors, and claude-first voter-1 semantics.

plan voter slots 2/3 always pass `--no-fallback` today, but the proposed registry schema documents only `review.panel` `paneldispatchpolicy` and omits plan-voter dispatch flags. without explicit `design.plan_voters` metadata and `test_external_role_defaults.py` pins, a registry refactor can drop always-on voter no-fallback or change slot tools without failing ci.

live plan-review `dispatch_panel` never passes `--no-fallback`; only `dispatch_voters` does (always). `review.panel` `paneldispatchpolicy` applies round-1-only panel no-fallback for code review only. shared `panel_dispatch_policy("review.panel")` wiring, missing `design.plan_review_panel` / `design.plan_voters` registry rows, or inline hardcoding can add panel-level no-fallback to plan review, drop voter-only no-fallback, or leave generic-codex round gates outside the registry.

`_load_dynamic_rows` emits one cursor and one codex row per scouted archetype from `scout-plan-manifest.json`. moving dynamic tool assignment into flat registry `slot_defaults` can break per-archetype dual-vendor expansion tied to the scout manifest.

when `codex_present` and `cursor_present` are both false, decompose panel dispatch uses a special claude generic launch branch before any `parallel_present` vendor manifest. `kind=parallel_present` `slot_defaults` cannot encode that branch; a registry-only rewrite can drop it and fail decompose when both externals are down.

the shared `scout dynamic-archetypes` cli has no role input, and the review pipeline still invokes it without one, so review and design scouts cannot select their distinct registry rows despite the helper signature split.

the plan says `python/review_aggregate.py` will choose `review.findings_aggregator` or `design.plan_findings_aggregator`, but `python/config.py` never registers either role or assigns a kind. both aggregators stay hardcoded and the single-source-of-truth goal is incomplete.

proposed `voterpolicydefault` omits live `archetype` and `default_label` fields even though `agent_voters` renders prompts from `policy.archetype` and falls back through `policy.default_label`. after registry migration, voter prompt rendering can lose `--archetype` values or fail to construct the live dataclass.

proposed `slotdefault` only stores slot/tool/labels while current generic code-review and plan-review rows set `model_role=default` per slot. rebuilding panel rows only from `slotdefault` can inherit dispatch `--model-role review` instead of `model_role=default`, breaking existing test pins.

python/agent_voters.py:183-188 [scope-reduction] `design.plan_voters` is assigned to `agent_voters.py`, but live plan voters dispatch only from `plan_review_panel.dispatch_voters` (`python/cli.py plan-review voter-dispatch`). `agent_voters.py` is code-review-only.. scenario: wiring `design.plan_voters` into `agent_voters.py` adds dead registry consumption and leaves `plan_review_panel.py:596-752` hardcoded, so plan-voter defaults stay grep-driven and the centralization goal fails for `/design` voters.

the plan has `design_lifecycle.py` call `resolve_vendor` with a `presence=` kwarg, but the proposed `external_defaults.py` contract uses `codex_present=` and `cursor_present=`. an implementer following the plan literally passes an undefined kwarg or invents a parallel api, breaking step 2b drafter selection or diverging from the resolver contract.

the plan tells `python/review_pipeline.py` to build static panel rows from `slot_defaults("review.panel")`, but the proposed `config.py` only registers `review.panel` `dispatch_policy` (no static specialist slot rows). registry migration can wire round-1 `--no-fallback` and generic-codex gating while `_append_static_specialist_rows` keeps hardcoded cursor/codex per `static_reviewers`, so code-review panel tool defaults stay grep-driven and fail the centralization goal.

`scout_plan_archetypes` subprocess-calls `scout dynamic-archetypes` without `--role-id`, but the plan makes `--role-id` required on that cli. once enforced, `scout plan-archetypes` / design step 2b scout wrapper fails before filter-manifest even though `review_pipeline` threads `review.dynamic_archetype_scout`; `design.plan_archetype_scout` defaults never apply on the live plan-scout path.

`design.decompose_panel` never gets a stable `role_id` in the canonical registry list. `python/decompose.py` is told to load the decompose panel from `external_defaults`, but there is no stable key to bind that lookup to, so the panel stays hardcoded or needs an ad hoc constant and registry centralization stays incomplete.

live step 2b sets `skip_reason=invalid-model` when `vendor=claude` and `larch_design_plan_model` is empty/whitespace, then falls through to inline drafting. the plan only documents `resolve_vendor` soft-fail for bad `larch_design_drafter` values. a naive `resolve_vendor` port can drop this branch and launch or hard-fail instead of inline fallback.

the plan splits `implement.ci_recovery_fixer` and `implement.rebase_conflict_fixer` and adds registry pins in `test_external_role_defaults.py`, but `test_agents.py`, `test_rebase.py`, `test_ci_monitor.py`, and `test_config.py` still key off shared `config.fixer_tier_order`. a compatibility alias derived from one role can keep those suites green when only the other role default changes, defeating independent-pin goal.

live `_static_slot_rows` runs a `render plan-review` subprocess for every archetype/vendor pair, then appends generic codex only for rounds 1–2. the plan says to build static specialist rows from `slot_defaults("design.plan_review_panel")`, which can be read as replacing that loop with flat registry rows and dropping prompt rendering.

the plan registers `design.brainstorm_framing` and `design.brainstorm_scope` but live step 1d.5 still hardcodes single-tool launch fences (`launch-review --tool cursor` / `--tool codex`) and a fixed tool-order table in `brainstorm.md`. the plan also mislabels these waterfall roles as `slot_defaults` even though they use tier order (`cursor→codex→claude` / `codex→cursor→claude`). registry or cli default changes would not move live launches; centralization stays split between registry tests and bash/prose dispatch.

skills/design/references/brainstorm.md:46-79 [scope-reduction] brainstorm framing/scope registry rows lack a python dispatch consumer. scenario: the plan registers `design.brainstorm_framing` / `design.brainstorm_scope` and updates prose to call `external-defaults`, but step 1d.5 still launches fixed cursor/codex commands from `brainstorm.md`. registry rows plus cli lookup add surface without changing live dispatch, so defaults can still drift from prose edits.

`design.plan_review_panel` static registry must pin plan-review archetypes (`arch`, `innovation`, `pragmatic`, `requirements`), not code-review `static_reviewers` (`correctness`, `edge-cases`, `testing`). `config.py` registers the latter explicitly for `review.panel` but only generic static rows for `design.plan_review_panel`, so an implementer can copy the code-review matrix and drop or mis-target the four plan-review specialists.

plan-review static migration must preserve cursor-always / codex-when-present row gating. live `_static_slot_rows` always appends cursor specialist rows and ignores `cursor_present`; codex rows are added only when `codex_present == "true"`. the plan says registry rows drive tools "with availability gates" but does not pin this asymmetry. gating cursor rows on `cursor_present` changes manifest shape and waterfall fallback behavior.

`review.panel` `slotdefault` schema omits manifest `agent` paths and generic-row `focus_area`/`weight`. live static rows set `"agent": agents/reviewer-{archetype}.md` and generic codex sets `agent`, `focus_area`, and `weight`. `_recount_manifest` and `_expected_static_slugs` key off `"agent" in row`. building manifest rows only from `slot`/`tool`/`model_role` drops static classification, breaks static slug coverage, and can break dispatch/collection. the plan says read tools from registry but keep "manifest-append structure" without naming `agent`/`output`; tool-only migration can drop `agent` from ndjson and break specialist launches.

`config.py` omits explicit registration for several waterfall roles that already have consumer repoints (`implement.step2_coder`, `implement.lint_fix_coder`, `review.fix_coder`, `design.plan_revision`, `review.dynamic_archetype_scout`, `design.plan_archetype_scout`). consumers are updated to `tool_order()`, but the `config.py` section only enumerates slot/voter/fixer subsets. new resolver calls would have no canonical data and would either fail or force ad hoc hardcoding.

decompose panel migration must keep per-archetype `_render_decompose_prompt` fan-out; registry must not replace the `decompose_archetypes` loop with flat `slot_defaults` rows. live dispatch builds manifest rows inside `for arch in decompose_archetypes` with per-archetype prompt rendering. flat registry rows can drop `_render_decompose_prompt` or the four archetypes (`decomposition-specialist`, `dependency-analyst`, `scope-minimalist`, `risk-isolation`).

`design.decompose_panel` registry lacks pinned parallel-vendor metadata beyond role existence. the plan tells `decompose.py` to load parallel dispatch from `slot_defaults("design.decompose_panel")`, but `config.py` bullets only require a firm `slot_panel` row with unspecified metadata. `test_external_role_defaults.py` pins existence only; `test_decompose.py` updates are may_update. the per-archetype loop can keep hardcoded `cursor`/`codex` rows, so changing the decompose default still requires grep edits and the role is not independently settable.

`design.plan_drafter` `resolve_vendor` inputs must preserve codex-on-path fallback when `codex_binary_found` is unset. live drafter selection uses `codex_binary_found == "true" or shutil.which("codex")` before choosing `codex` vs `claude`. the plan shows `resolve_vendor(..., codex_present=...)` but does not require the caller to keep the `which("codex")` fallback when session env is empty. passing session presence only can skip the drafter and change step 2b inline-fallback behavior on path-only codex installs.

step 2 coder migration does not pin first-eligible single-vendor selection semantics. live `_phase_coder` picks exactly one implementer from `codex→cursor→claude` availability (or explicit `--coder` reordering). the plan routes `implement.step2_coder` through `tool_order()` but never states that bootstrap must keep pick-one behavior rather than lint-fix-style sequential attempts across vendors. an implementer can copy the multi-attempt loop from `checks.run_lint_fix` and change step 2 dispatch/fallback semantics.

fixer split behavioral pins remain `may_update` only (prior round-3 finding_6 incomplete). `test_external_role_defaults.py` pins registry tuples, but `test_agents.py`, `test_rebase.py`, and `test_ci_monitor.py` still parametrize on shared `config.fixer_tier_order`. a deprecated alias derived from one fixer role can keep those suites green when only the other role default changes, defeating the issue's independent-pin goal.

python/decompose.py:445-455 [scope-reduction] `design.decompose_panel` registry migration omits the per-archetype `_render_decompose_prompt` contract.. scenario: live `dispatch_panel` loops `decompose_archetypes`, calls `_render_decompose_prompt` per archetype/vendor, and writes manifest rows with `prompt_file` before `dispatch-waterfall`. the plan only says to load parallel tools from `slot_defaults("design.decompose_panel")` and keep the both-absent claude branch; it never states that registry rows are tool metadata only or that the render loop must stay. a flat `slot_defaults` manifest without per-archetype prompts breaks decompose launches.

`design.decompose_panel` migration must preserve per-vendor presence gating inside the archetype loop. live `dispatch_panel` adds a cursor row only when `cursor_present` and a codex row only when `codex_present`; one-vendor-down runs are not parallel dual-vendor manifests. the plan pins `parallel_tools=("cursor","codex")` and says to expand rows from that tuple, which can be read as always emitting both tools whenever any external is present.

`review.panel` static migration must preserve asymmetric specialist-row gating. live `_append_static_specialist_rows` always appends cursor specialist rows and adds codex rows only when `codex_slots_available`. building static rows from flat `slot_defaults("review.panel")` without the same asymmetry changes manifest shape and waterfall fallback when cursor is down or codex is absent.

`scout_plan_archetypes_scout_sh` override must keep forwarding `--role-id` on the inner argv. tests stub the inner scout via `scout_plan_archetypes_scout_sh`. the plan requires `--role-id` on nested `scout dynamic-archetypes`, but it does not state that the override path still appends the full argv tail (including `--role-id`) when `scout_cmd` is replaced.

`design.plan_voters` migration omits per-slot availability gating for voter-2/voter-3 manifest rows. live `dispatch_voters` adds voter-2 only when `codex_available=="true"` and voter-3 only when `cursor_available=="true"` before `--no-fallback` waterfall. the plan says to build voter-2/voter-3 rows from `voter_policies("design.plan_voters")` but never pins this asymmetric inclusion. a registry-driven loop that always emits both policy rows can launch the wrong voter set when only one external is present.

code-review voter dispatch must preserve `external_voter23` manifest shape and omit `--no-fallback`. live `agent_voters.dispatch_voters` includes voter-2 and voter-3 waterfall rows whenever either external is present (`external_voter23`), and `_dispatch_waterfall` never passes `--no-fallback` (unlike plan voters). the plan migrates `review.voters` policies but does not state these dispatch semantics. a shared voter-dispatch helper copied from `plan_review_panel.dispatch_voters` could shrink the manifest to one row or add always-on `--no-fallback`, breaking codex-primary slots 2/3 waterfall fallback.

firm scout `--role-id` cli enforcement still lacks firm test pins. the plan makes `--role-id` required on `scout dynamic-archetypes` and `scout plan-archetypes` and requires nested forwarding from `scout_plan_archetypes`, but the only test coverage is `may_update: python/test_plan_scout.py`. an implementer can skip may_update updates and ship a cli/schema change without ci failing on missing argv or nested subprocess forwarding.

missing consumer test for the new aggregator role split. registry tests alone will not catch a hardcoded cursor slot, so plan review aggregation can still use the wrong tool for `--input-mode plan` while ci stays green.
